name: Take It Abroad!

pick.label: Pick something German
pick.heading: Pick something very German and launch it in another country
lead: Some things are so German that nobody outside Germany has ever heard of them. Others have travelled the world, and some had to change quite a lot on the way.
Choose something from the shelf (or your own idea), choose a country, and work out how to make people there love it. *What changes, and what stays the same?*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a perfect export strategy here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some launches will make total sense, and some will be a beautiful disaster. Both are welcome.

rows: Which German thing are you exporting?
The name, the look, the taste, the story… What would confuse people there?
What has to stay, or it isn’t really German any more?
Its new name, if it needs one. Is it easy to say there?
Where does it appear first, and who talks about it?

values.thing: Sandmännchen, the little man who has been sending German children to bed since 1959.
values.where: Scotland, because Scottish children are just as good at refusing to go to bed.
values.change: He comes on just before seven in the evening, but in June it’s still light in Edinburgh at ten o’clock. So he brings blackout curtains and a very good excuse.
values.keep: The beard, the pointy hat and the sand. Also the slightly strange vehicles: he arrives on a ferry from Orkney.
values.name: The Wee Sandman. Easy to say, and nobody needs to try “Männchen”.
values.launch: On children’s TV, and with a stuffed toy at every station, so tired parents can buy him on the way home.

yours.label: Your launch
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your launch in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which launch wins?
